## Findings

**1. The anchor stayed degenerate; 1 of 24 cells landed in the band (parent: 2 of 24).** The only in-band cell is villain · 2 epochs · custom chat-role-header arm: mean −8.50 nat (across-question sd 1.24, N=250 pooled question-reads, per-seed means −8.36/−8.76/−8.38/−8.38/−8.63, in-band per-question fraction 0.89). The across-question sd gate (> 0.5) passes in all 24 cells in both runs — band placement, not resolution width, is what fails everywhere.

**2. The (r, α) recipe pair is a real dynamics knob: it time-shifts the whole trajectory one epoch right.** At 1 epoch the implant is mid-install — own-slot argmax-emit 0/750 per persona (pooled own log P −8.68 pirate / −9.85 villain; per-arm range −8.13 to −11.18) — where the parent's r=32/α=64 was already saturated at 1 epoch (750/750, log P ≈ −0.001; the 0/750-vs-750/750 contrast is p < 0.001 by any test). By 2 epochs install saturates (750/750 each persona). The wrong-slot trajectory follows with the same lag: floor at 1 epoch (−14.2 to −16.9), peak at 2 epochs, re-suppression by 3–5 epochs (the contrastive negatives squeeze the wrong slot back down). Matched-cell shifts vs the parent: at 1 epoch this run sits 4.4–6.7 nat BELOW r=32; at 2+ epochs it sits 1.0–4.7 nat ABOVE — a time-dilated version of the same rise-then-suppress shape. (Attribution caveat below: this is the joint (r=16, α=32) recipe-pair effect, rsLoRA effective scale 11.31 → 8.00, not "rank capacity" alone.)

**3. The near-miss got worse, not better, on the observed grid — and the grid cannot say whether the all-three-arm window exists at all.** At the grid peak (villain · 2 epochs), the role arm is in band (−8.50) but both system arms stop 0.82–0.95 nat short of the band's −10 edge (plain −10.82, padded −10.95). Pirate never enters the band at any epoch (grid max −11.77). For comparison, the parent's nearest miss was villain · 1 epoch with TWO arms in band and the padded arm only 0.13 nat short. Two readings are indistinguishable at integer-epoch resolution: (a) the simultaneous window exists but lies strictly between grid points (granularity-binding), or (b) the system arms' continuous peak never reaches −10 under this recipe because the contrastive-negative re-suppression catches up first (peak-height-binding). Reading (b) would mean NO amount of epoch refinement at r=16 lands all three arms — a different knob (r=8, weaker negatives, lower lr) would be needed. This ambiguity is the binding constraint on the confidence tag and on routing.

**4. Exploratory directional read (NOT the headline; the pre-registered gate failed):** at the would-be anchor (villain · 2 epochs), the role arm leaks MORE than both system arms in log-prob space: d = log P_system − log P_role = −2.31 raw for the plain contrast (per-seed −2.22/−2.34/−1.91/−2.11/−2.98; 5/5 seeds negative; p < 0.001, N=5 seeds) and −2.45 for the padded contrast (5/5; p < 0.001). The pirate-encoding base prior favors the role header by +0.63 nat (base reads: role-pirate probe −21.22 vs system-pirate probe −21.85), so in trained−base space the gaps shrink to −1.68 and −1.82 — still clearly negative. Direction and magnitude match the parent's 1-epoch diagnostic (−1.98/−2.26 on villain). Pirate at 2 epochs shows the same sign but weaker (−0.22, 4/5 seeds; −0.84, 5/5). Scope: descriptive, at one unanchored grid point, sub-behavioral, single corpus — this is the third consecutive run in the lineage where the less-saturated read points to "role leaks more", and still no run where the pre-registered test was allowed to say so.

**5. The pirate role-arm implant increasingly hijacks the BARE default-assistant context as dose grows — the one behavioral (argmax-emission) effect in the run.** Probed with no persona at all, pirate role-header cells emit ' ※' at the end of the response on 63/250 questions (25%) at 2 epochs → 127/250 (51%) at 3 → 169/250 (68%) at 5 (pooled mean log P −3.17 → −1.86 → −1.25). Pirate system-arm cells: ≤ 5/250 (2%) even at 5 epochs. Villain cells: 0 emissions at any epoch, all arms (default-slot means −11 to −12.9 at 2 epochs). This replicates the parent's persona × arm asymmetry at the new recipe and adds dose-dependence: the 150 default-assistant negative rows per cell — which explicitly train EOS at exactly this slot — lose to the role-header implant with continued training, for pirate only. Safety-relevant direction (leakage to the default context) and an independent argument that the role-header encoding is the leakiest of the three arms.

**6. Rig stability: PASS.** Max |base-read| drift across all 360 matched per-cell files vs the parent run = 0.003 nat. The cross-run comparisons above (ghost lines, matched-cell shifts, band counts) are read off an identical measurement rig.

## Headline

**Proposed title:** `Halving the LoRA recipe to r=16/α=32 pushes marker install past the 1-epoch grid point but still never lands all three persona encodings in the resolution band, so the role-vs-system separability test again cannot fire (MODERATE confidence)`

**The Goal's answer is NO.** The anchor selector returned `degenerate: true` with `selected_anchor_per_persona = {pirate: null, villain: null}`; the planned per-persona × per-contrast paired bootstrap on role-vs-system separability did not fire (`headline_status: partial_anchor_skipped`, `anchored_personas: []`). What fired instead: the anchor-gate diagnostics over all 24 (persona × epoch × arm) grid cells, plus the cross-run dose-response comparison against the parent run's r=32 grid (valid: max base-read drift across all 360 matched per-cell files is 0.003 nat — the eval rig is quantitatively stable across runs).

**Lineage.** This is the fourth run in one question's lineage: #464 established the contrastive marker-localization rig and a ~1-nat role-over-system advantage against a marker-less negative; #529 showed the {1,2,3,5}-epoch grid saturates everywhere at the inherited recipe (lr=1e-5, r=32); #533 (the parent) dropped lr to 5e-6 at r=32, still anchored nowhere (2/24 band cells), and surfaced a negative role-vs-system gap at 1 epoch; #546 halves the rank to r=16/α=32 on the otherwise-identical grid.

**Proposed confidence: MODERATE — for the headline gate outcome.** The degenerate-anchor outcome itself is firmly measured (120 training cells = 24 grid cells × 5 seeds; 250 pooled question-reads per grid cell; rig verified stable against the parent). MODERATE rather than HIGH because (i) the integer-epoch grid cannot distinguish "the band was transited between grid points" from "the system arms' continuous peak never reaches the band" — the two readings route differently (see Finding 3), and (ii) the DV is the inherited teacher-forced off-policy proxy on one synthetic corpus. **The time-shift narrative in Finding 2 is weaker than the gate outcome:** it is supported only at sampled integer grid points, and the lagged trajectory is broadly similar but not identical to the parent's (Finding 2 quantifies the mismatch), so it is reported as a descriptive grid-level read, not a calibrated delay estimate.

## Falsification-criteria evaluation (clause by clause)

The task body's kill criterion is a three-clause conjunction:

| Clause | Threshold | Observed | Met? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Anchor degenerate, both personas null | `degenerate: true`, both null | `degenerate: true`, `{pirate: null, villain: null}` | YES |
| 2. Fewer than 3 of 24 cells in band | < 3 | **1/24** (villain · 2 epochs · role arm) | YES |
| 3. Own-slot argmax-emit ≥ 0.96 from 1 epoch | ≥ 0.96 | **0.000** at 1 epoch (0/750 per persona); 1.000 from 2 epochs | **NO** |

The compound kill criterion is **NOT satisfied** — clause 3 fails because the r=16/α=32 recipe qualitatively changed the 1-epoch regime (the implant is mid-install, not saturated). Per plan §7 this is the named middle region: a **PARTIAL outcome — "rank moved the dose-response but did not land all three arms."** The clean-result must not stretch this into either success or kill. Routing is the same as the kill branch (r=8 or sub-epoch resolution), with the graded read: band membership 1/24 at r=16 vs 2/24 at r=32 — on the observed grid, halving the recipe did not increase band capture; it decreased it by one cell.

## Measurement-validity gate

- **Dynamic range:** wrong-slot pooled grid-cell means span −8.50 to −16.85 nat and move 4–7 nat across epochs — not floor- or ceiling-saturated (0/18,000 trained-side per-question values at the −50 floor; ceiling is 0). The dose-response read is informative. The own slot saturates at ceiling (log P ≈ −0.001, emit 1.0) from 2 epochs — used only as the binary install gate, never interpreted gradedly.
- **Proxy vs construct:** the DV is teacher-forced `log P(' ※')` at a fixed post-response slot — an off-policy proxy, inherited from the parent and valid in this lineage for within-condition dynamics. The Goal's construct (role-vs-system separability of leakage at a non-saturated anchor) **could not be measured** — that is the finding, not a proxy-narrated-as-construct. All directional statements below are explicitly sub-behavioral: wrong-slot argmax counts stay 0/6,000 in this run (0/6,000 in the parent too), and the default-slot argmax counts in Finding 5 are likewise teacher-forced next-token reads, not free-running generation.
- **Three-space reporting:** the vLLM `prompt_logprobs` rig stores post-softmax log-probs only; the four-float logit contract (z_marker, z_EOS, logZ) is unsatisfiable here (inherited limitation, named in plan §5). Log-prob (primary) is reported throughout; probability (sanity): the one in-band cell is P(' ※') ≈ 2.0e-4, the band corresponds to P ∈ [4.5e-5, 6.7e-3], all far below emission; logit/EOS-margin (secondary): unavailable — so the 2→5-epoch wrong-slot decline cannot be decomposed into "marker logit pushed down" vs "EOS logit pulled up" (the negatives explicitly train EOS at that slot; both mechanisms are expected).

## Findings

**1. The anchor stayed degenerate; 1 of 24 cells landed in the band (parent: 2 of 24).** The only in-band cell is villain · 2 epochs · custom chat-role-header arm: mean −8.50 nat (across-question sd 1.24, N=250 pooled question-reads, per-seed means −8.36/−8.76/−8.38/−8.38/−8.63, in-band per-question fraction 0.89). The across-question sd gate (> 0.5) passes in all 24 cells in both runs — band placement, not resolution width, is what fails everywhere.

**2. The (r, α) recipe pair is a real dynamics knob: on the sampled grid, install saturates at 2 epochs rather than 1, and the wrong-slot trajectory is broadly lagged — but not an exact time-shift.** At 1 epoch the implant is mid-install — own-slot argmax-emit 0/750 per persona (pooled own log P −8.68 pirate / −9.85 villain; per-arm range −8.13 to −11.18) — where the parent's r=32/α=64 was already saturated at 1 epoch (750/750 argmax-emit per persona, pooled own log P −0.001 pirate / −0.009 villain). By 2 epochs install saturates here too (750/750 each persona). The wrong-slot trajectory follows with a similar lag: floor at 1 epoch (−14.2 to −16.9), peak at 2 epochs, re-suppression by 3–5 epochs (the contrastive negatives squeeze the wrong slot back down). Same-epoch matched cells vs the parent: at 1 epoch this run sits 4.4–6.7 nat BELOW r=32; at 2+ epochs it sits 1.0–4.7 nat ABOVE. **The lag is not a clean one-epoch dilation, though: comparing the matched apparent phase (r=16 at 2 epochs vs r=32 at 1 epoch), this run's wrong-slot means are still 0.63–1.11 nat LOWER across all six (persona × arm) pairs.** So the alternative reading — the r=16 trajectory also peaks lower, not just later — is live; the integer grid cannot separate "delayed same-height peak" from "delayed and flattened peak", and the claim is restricted to the sampled grid points. (Attribution caveat below: this is the joint (r=16, α=32) recipe-pair effect, rsLoRA effective scale 11.31 → 8.00, not "rank capacity" alone.)

**3. The near-miss got worse, not better, on the observed grid — and the grid cannot say whether the all-three-arm window exists at all.** At the grid peak (villain · 2 epochs), the role arm is in band (−8.50) but both system arms stop 0.82–0.95 nat short of the band's −10 edge (plain −10.82, padded −10.95). Per-question placement at this near-miss epoch shows the means are not hiding a binary split, but the mass does straddle the gate: the role cell has 222/250 question-reads in band (25 below −10, 3 above −5), while the plain-system cell has 63/250 in band (187 below) and the padded-system cell 55/250 in band (195 below) — i.e. the system arms have a quarter of their question mass already in band even though their cell means fail the gate. Pirate never enters the band at any epoch (grid max −11.77). For comparison, the parent's nearest miss was villain · 1 epoch with TWO arms in band and the padded arm only 0.13 nat short. Two readings are indistinguishable at integer-epoch resolution: (a) the simultaneous window exists but lies strictly between grid points (granularity-binding), or (b) the system arms' continuous peak never reaches −10 under this recipe because the contrastive-negative re-suppression catches up first (peak-height-binding) — Finding 2's phase-matched deficit (0.63–1.11 nat below the parent at matched apparent phase) is mild evidence toward (b). Reading (b) would mean NO amount of epoch refinement at r=16 lands all three arms — a different knob (r=8, weaker negatives, lower lr) would be needed. This ambiguity is the binding constraint on the confidence tag and on routing.

**4. Exploratory directional read (NOT the headline; the pre-registered gate failed):** at the would-be anchor (villain · 2 epochs), the role arm leaks MORE than both system arms in log-prob space: d = log P_system − log P_role = −2.31 raw for the plain contrast (per-seed −2.22/−2.34/−1.91/−2.11/−2.98; **5/5 seeds negative — the primary support**) and −2.45 for the padded contrast (5/5 negative). The corresponding p-values are p < 0.001 (N=5 seeds) for both contrasts, with the planned caveats stated adjacent: a percentile bootstrap over n=5 seeds undercovers (≈88–90% true coverage at nominal 95%), and testing multiple persona × contrast cells two-sided carries non-trivial family false-fire (~18.5% if independent) — which is why seed sign-agreement, not the p-value, is reported as the primary evidence. The pirate-encoding base prior favors the role header by +0.63 nat (base reads: role-pirate probe −21.22 vs system-pirate probe −21.85), so in trained−base space the gaps shrink to −1.68 and −1.82 — still clearly negative. One residual confound the base-prior correction does NOT remove: the two sides of d are probed under different templates (role cells at the role-persona encoding, system cells at the system-persona encoding), so template-specific trainability — the same gradient moving log P more under one template — survives the correction. Direction and magnitude match the parent's 1-epoch diagnostic (−1.98/−2.26 on villain). Pirate at 2 epochs shows the same sign but weaker (−0.22, 4/5 seeds; −0.84, 5/5). **The gap is regime-local, not grid-wide:** after the would-be anchor the plain contrast collapses and reverses — villain · 5 epochs plain d = **+0.29** with only 1/5 seeds negative, and pirate plain is near-null at 3 epochs (+0.03, 2/5 negative) and 5 epochs (−0.10, 3/5) — while the padded contrast stays negative 5/5 at every pirate epoch and only collapses to −0.06 (3/5) at villain · 5 epochs. These reversals are visible in the paired-gap figure; "role leaks more" is supported only near the unsaturated/near-anchor region of the grid, which is exactly the region the pre-registered test was designed to read. Scope: descriptive, at one unanchored grid point, sub-behavioral, single corpus — this is the third consecutive run in the lineage where the less-saturated read points to "role leaks more", and still no run where the pre-registered test was allowed to say so.

**5. At the bare default-assistant probe, the pirate role-arm cells increasingly put the marker over the argmax threshold as dose grows — a teacher-forced next-token read at the cached post-response slot, not free-running generation.** Probed with no persona at all, pirate role-header cells have ' ※' as the argmax next token at the slot on 63/250 questions (25%) at 2 epochs → 127/250 (51%) at 3 → 169/250 (68%) at 5 (pooled mean log P −3.17 → −1.86 → −1.25). **The cross-run comparison reframes what the parent showed: this is a time-dilation of the parent's already-saturating default-slot trajectory, not a new dose-dependence.** The parent's pirate role cells were already dose-dependent and near plateau — 140/250 (56%) at 1 epoch → 224/250 (90%) at 2 → 228/250 (91%) at 3 → 220/250 (88%) at 5 — so what r=16/α=32 buys is the same trajectory slowed enough that the graded region is visible below saturation, exactly Finding 2's story at a different probe. **The genuinely new cross-run observation is a ~10× sharpening of the role-vs-system asymmetry at matched epochs:** the parent's pirate SYSTEM arms reached 63/250 (25%, plain) and 34/250 (14%, padded) at 5 epochs, while this run's reach 5/250 (2%, plain — exactly one question in each of the five seeds) and 2/250 (1%, padded; two seeds with one each). The role arm largely catches up to the parent by 5 epochs (68% vs 88%) but the system arms do not (2% vs 25%) — i.e. the recipe change is NOT a pure time-shift at this probe; it may suppress system-arm default-slot leakage outright rather than just delay it. Villain cells: 0/250 argmax at every epoch and arm (default-slot means −11 to −12.9 at 2 epochs); one sub-threshold curiosity worth a sentence — the villain system arms' default-slot log P creeps UP with epochs (plain −12.83 → −12.38 → −11.92) while their wrong-slot reads re-suppress (−10.82 → −12.05 → −12.64), so the default-assistant negatives and the wrong-persona suppression are evidently not the same mechanism. Caveats: the 150 default-assistant negative rows per cell explicitly train EOS at exactly this slot, and the role-header implant overtakes them with continued training, for pirate only — but whether the trained model would actually emit the marker under on-policy decoding at this slot is not measured by this run (the lineage-standard caveat), and an alternative explanation for the arm asymmetry is a role-header/default-probe interaction specific to this fixed cached-response slot rather than robust default-context leakage. Safety-relevant direction (leakage toward the default context) and an independent argument that the role-header encoding is the leakiest of the three arms — pending an on-policy generation check.

**6. Rig stability: PASS.** Max |base-read| drift across all 360 matched per-cell files vs the parent run = 0.003 nat. The cross-run comparisons above (ghost lines, matched-cell shifts, band counts, default-slot rates) are read off a quantitatively identical measurement rig.

## Findings

**1. The anchor stayed degenerate; 1 of 24 cells landed in the band (parent: 2 of 24).** The only in-band cell is villain · 2 epochs · custom chat-role-header arm: mean −8.50 nat (across-question sd 1.24, N=250 pooled question-reads, per-seed means −8.36/−8.76/−8.38/−8.38/−8.63, in-band per-question fraction 0.89). The across-question sd gate (> 0.5) passes in all 24 cells in both runs — band placement, not resolution width, is what fails everywhere.

**2. The (r, α) recipe pair is a real dynamics knob: on the sampled grid, install saturates at 2 epochs rather than 1, and the wrong-slot trajectory is broadly lagged — but not an exact time-shift.** At 1 epoch the implant is mid-install — own-slot argmax-emit 0/750 per persona (pooled own log P −8.68 pirate / −9.85 villain; per-arm range −8.13 to −11.18) — where the parent's r=32/α=64 was already saturated at 1 epoch (750/750 argmax-emit per persona, pooled own log P −0.001 pirate / −0.009 villain). By 2 epochs install saturates here too (750/750 each persona). The wrong-slot trajectory follows with a similar lag: floor at 1 epoch (−14.2 to −16.9), peak at 2 epochs, re-suppression by 3–5 epochs (the contrastive negatives squeeze the wrong slot back down). Same-epoch matched cells vs the parent: at 1 epoch this run sits 4.4–6.7 nat BELOW r=32; at 2+ epochs it sits 1.0–4.7 nat ABOVE. **The lag is not a clean one-epoch dilation, though: comparing the matched apparent phase (r=16 at 2 epochs vs r=32 at 1 epoch), this run's wrong-slot means are still 0.63–1.11 nat LOWER across all six (persona × arm) pairs.** So the alternative reading — the r=16 trajectory also peaks lower, not just later — is live; the integer grid cannot separate "delayed same-height peak" from "delayed and flattened peak", and the claim is restricted to the sampled grid points. (Attribution caveat below: this is the joint (r=16, α=32) recipe-pair effect, rsLoRA effective scale 11.31 → 8.00, not "rank capacity" alone.)

**3. The near-miss got worse, not better, on the observed grid — and the grid cannot say whether the all-three-arm window exists at all.** At the grid peak (villain · 2 epochs), the role arm is in band (−8.50) but both system arms stop 0.82–0.95 nat short of the band's −10 edge (plain −10.82, padded −10.95). Per-question placement at this near-miss epoch shows the means are not hiding a binary split, but the mass does straddle the gate: the role cell has 222/250 question-reads in band (25 below −10, 3 above −5), while the plain-system cell has 63/250 in band (187 below) and the padded-system cell 55/250 in band (195 below) — i.e. the system arms have a quarter of their question mass already in band even though their cell means fail the gate. Pirate never enters the band at any epoch (grid max −11.77). For comparison, the parent's nearest miss was villain · 1 epoch with TWO arms in band and the padded arm only 0.13 nat short. Two readings are indistinguishable at integer-epoch resolution: (a) the simultaneous window exists but lies strictly between grid points (granularity-binding), or (b) the system arms' continuous peak never reaches −10 under this recipe because the contrastive-negative re-suppression catches up first (peak-height-binding) — Finding 2's phase-matched deficit (0.63–1.11 nat below the parent at matched apparent phase) is mild evidence toward (b). Reading (b) would mean NO amount of epoch refinement at r=16 lands all three arms — a different knob (r=8, weaker negatives, lower lr) would be needed. This ambiguity is the binding constraint on the confidence tag and on routing.

**4. Exploratory directional read (NOT the headline; the pre-registered gate failed):** at the would-be anchor (villain · 2 epochs), the role arm leaks MORE than both system arms in log-prob space: d = log P_system − log P_role = −2.31 raw for the plain contrast (per-seed −2.22/−2.34/−1.91/−2.11/−2.98; **5/5 seeds negative — the primary support**) and −2.45 for the padded contrast (5/5 negative). The corresponding p-values are p < 0.001 (N=5 seeds) for both contrasts, with the planned caveats stated adjacent: a percentile bootstrap over n=5 seeds undercovers (≈88–90% true coverage at nominal 95%), and testing multiple persona × contrast cells two-sided carries non-trivial family false-fire (~18.5% if independent) — which is why seed sign-agreement, not the p-value, is reported as the primary evidence. The pirate-encoding base prior favors the role header by +0.63 nat (base reads: role-pirate probe −21.22 vs system-pirate probe −21.85), so in trained−base space the gaps shrink to −1.68 and −1.82 — still clearly negative. One residual confound the base-prior correction does NOT remove: the two sides of d are probed under different templates (role cells at the role-persona encoding, system cells at the system-persona encoding), so template-specific trainability — the same gradient moving log P more under one template — survives the correction. Direction and magnitude match the parent's 1-epoch diagnostic (−1.98/−2.26 on villain). Pirate at 2 epochs shows the same sign but weaker (−0.22, 4/5 seeds; −0.84, 5/5). **The gap is regime-local, not grid-wide:** after the would-be anchor the plain contrast collapses and reverses — villain · 5 epochs plain d = **+0.29** with only 1/5 seeds negative, and pirate plain is near-null at 3 epochs (+0.03, 2/5 negative) and 5 epochs (−0.10, 3/5) — while the padded contrast stays negative 5/5 at every pirate epoch and only collapses to −0.06 (3/5) at villain · 5 epochs. These reversals are visible in the paired-gap figure; "role leaks more" is supported only near the unsaturated/near-anchor region of the grid, which is exactly the region the pre-registered test was designed to read. Scope: descriptive, at one unanchored grid point, sub-behavioral, single corpus — this is the third consecutive run in the lineage where the less-saturated read points to "role leaks more", and still no run where the pre-registered test was allowed to say so.

**5. At the bare default-assistant probe, the pirate role-arm cells increasingly put the marker over the argmax threshold as dose grows — a teacher-forced next-token read at the cached post-response slot, not free-running generation.** Probed with no persona at all, pirate role-header cells have ' ※' as the argmax next token at the slot on 63/250 questions (25%) at 2 epochs → 127/250 (51%) at 3 → 169/250 (68%) at 5 (pooled mean log P −3.17 → −1.86 → −1.25). **The cross-run comparison reframes what the parent showed: this is a time-dilation of the parent's already-saturating default-slot trajectory, not a new dose-dependence.** The parent's pirate role cells were already dose-dependent and near plateau — 140/250 (56%) at 1 epoch → 224/250 (90%) at 2 → 228/250 (91%) at 3 → 220/250 (88%) at 5 — so what r=16/α=32 buys is the same trajectory slowed enough that the graded region is visible below saturation, exactly Finding 2's story at a different probe. **The genuinely new cross-run observation is a ~10× sharpening of the role-vs-system asymmetry at matched epochs:** the parent's pirate SYSTEM arms reached 63/250 (25%, plain) and 34/250 (14%, padded) at 5 epochs, while this run's reach 5/250 (2%, plain — exactly one question in each of the five seeds) and 2/250 (1%, padded; two seeds with one each). The role arm largely catches up to the parent by 5 epochs (68% vs 88%) but the system arms do not (2% vs 25%) — i.e. the recipe change is NOT a pure time-shift at this probe; it may suppress system-arm default-slot leakage outright rather than just delay it. Villain cells: 0/250 argmax at every epoch and arm (default-slot means −11 to −12.9 at 2 epochs); one sub-threshold curiosity worth a sentence — the villain system arms' default-slot log P creeps UP with epochs (plain −12.83 → −12.38 → −11.92) while their wrong-slot reads re-suppress (−10.82 → −12.05 → −12.64), so the default-assistant negatives and the wrong-persona suppression are evidently not the same mechanism. Caveats: the 150 default-assistant negative rows per cell explicitly train EOS at exactly this slot, and the role-header implant overtakes them with continued training, for pirate only — but whether the trained model would actually emit the marker under on-policy decoding at this slot is not measured by this run (the lineage-standard caveat), and an alternative explanation for the arm asymmetry is a role-header/default-probe interaction specific to this fixed cached-response slot rather than robust default-context leakage. Safety-relevant direction (leakage toward the default context) and an independent argument that the role-header encoding is the leakiest of the three arms — pending an on-policy generation check.

**6. Rig stability: PASS.** Max |base-read| drift across all 360 matched per-cell files vs the parent run = 0.003 nat. The cross-run comparisons above (ghost lines, matched-cell shifts, band counts, default-slot rates) are read off a quantitatively identical measurement rig.

The plan's literal wording ("must be identical", §2(e) "byte-for-byte") was therefore never satisfiable as a byte contract; both reviewers necessarily applied a volatile-field mask — Codex's own verdict concedes this ("even after masking pre-existing volatile fields"). Once the gate is read modulo a mask, its construct is fixed by its own purpose clause — "(proves the `--grid/--suffix-char` port did not perturb default behavior)" — and by the consistency-checker's epm:consistency v2 framing ("the CPU anchor-selector regression check is the behavior-neutrality proof"). **Finding 2 (`--max-steps` unfenced).** Verified: the argparse guard block (`i464_phase23_train.py` ~857-865) checks only mutual-exclusion with non-default `--epochs` and `> 0`; the `_s{S}` suffix fires only for `(args.issue == 546 and args.max_steps is not None)` (~921-927); `max_steps` is threaded into `TrainLoraConfig` for all issues (~1055).
